titleEn: Oṃ is a, u, m — and the silence after. Waking, dream, deep sleep, and the one who watches.
meaningEn: Oṃ is one sound that holds three. A, U and M run together into one, and then there is a silence. The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad says: A is the waking world, U is the dream, M is dreamless sleep — and the silence after is the fourth, the awareness in which all three come and go.
meaningHi: ॐ एक आवाज़ है जिसमें तीन आवाज़ें हैं — अ, उ, म — और फिर चुप्पी। माण्डूक्य उपनिषद कहता है: अ जागना है, उ सपना है, म गहरी नींद है — और उसके बाद की चुप्पी चौथी है, वह जो तीनों को आते-जाते देखता है।
sayItLike: om — 'o' as in 'home', then the m hums and fades into silence

words.glossEn: the first sound — the waking world
words.grammar: Māṇḍūkya 9: a-kāra is Vaiśvānara, the waking self
Māṇḍūkya 10: u-kāra is Taijasa, the dreaming self

words.glossEn: the third sound — deep, dreamless sleep
words.grammar: Māṇḍūkya 11: ma-kāra is Prājña, the self in deep sleep

words.glossEn: the fourth — no sound at all; the silence after
words.glossHi: चौथा — कोई आवाज़ नहीं; बाद की चुप्पी
words.root: a + mātrā — 'without measure', the text's own word for the soundless fourth
words.grammar: Māṇḍūkya 12: the part with no measure is Turīya, the fourth

source.ref: 1 and 8–12 (a = waking, u = dream, m = deep sleep; the measureless fourth); also Kaṭha 1.2.15–16, Taittirīya 1.8, Bhagavad Gītā 8.13
source.note: The three-sounds-and-silence reading is the Māṇḍūkya's own, not a later gloss. That a + u + m sound as 'o' is ordinary Sanskrit sandhi — which is why the letter is written ओ with a mark, not अउम.

significance.textSays: Māṇḍūkya 1: 'Oṃ — this syllable is all this.' Verses 9–12 lay a, u, m over waking, dream and deep sleep, and the soundless fourth over the Self that knows all three.
significance.traditionSays: Opens every mantra and every reading of scripture; the Gītā (8.13) calls it the one-syllable Brahman — and the silence the Upaniṣad names is part of the sound itself.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That the sound does anything on its own. The text says what the sound means; that is quoted here, and no more.
